# HyperFrames keyframes — seek-safe motion design

Curated by Skill Harbor — a motion-design skill by @heygen-com for the HyperFrames composition framework: it treats keyframes as a pose contract (visible states, continuous subject identity, seek-safe runtime, verified pixels) and maps creator requests to truthful mechanisms — punch-in/out, multi-state zooms, pan and Ken Burns moves, match cuts and whip pans, mask/crop reframes, split-screen handoffs, freeze holds. Includes hard runtime rules (synchronous builds, registered timelines, finite durations, no Date.now/timers/async randomness for render-critical motion), channel preferences (compositor channels like x/y/scale/opacity/clip-path over layout channels), mechanism-choice and timing guidance, SVG/canvas/3D notes, a CLI proof ladder (`hyperframes lint`, `check`, `keyframes`, `--shot`, snapshots), and an error-handling table. Honest caveats: it is one piece of the HyperFrames ecosystem — clip assembly belongs to `/hyperframes-core`, sound to `/hyperframes-audio`; the skill explicitly states what it does NOT do (face tracking, automatic semantic reframing, automatic matching-frame discovery). Credit to its creator. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
